complexity.notes: Non-idiomatic counting (use dict.get(num, 0) + 1 or collections.Counter) and the reverse lookup re-scans the dict up to k times instead of sorting items by frequency directly. Also, when multiple keys share a frequency, the set-deduped result can return more than k elements, and duplicate frequencies in the sliced list cause redundant scans.
complexity.summary: Builds a frequency map with a dict, sorts the frequency values and keeps the top k (k <= 5, so bounded), then for each retained frequency scans the whole dict to recover matching keys, deduplicating with a set at the end.
